{"self_assessment": "Impact: I chose the concept and set the plan in the first minute: a left-facing fish with a forked tail, chosen because its outline reads at a glance. I sketched it on the pad and assigned strokes so all four of us were building at once. I laid the start domino and the full top line, the longest single stroke and the backbone of the body. When the nose join wasn't catching, I laid the connect that linked the start run into the top line. At last check, about 199 of the 247 standing dominoes were connected to the start.

Execution: I stayed on the critical path. I finished the top line, then inspected the nose and the notch rather than assuming they were fine. I identified the two open ends in the notch so the join went to the right spots. I cleared stray, unconnected dominoes and lifted pale strays past the tail. That returned dominoes to the shared pile when supply ran short, and I handed spares to Maya for the final join.

Collaboration: I kept the table informed throughout, with short status updates and clear handoffs, and I told people where my hands were so we didn't bump each other. I stayed off the notch while Maya worked there. I also thanked teammates for their catches, such as Tom spotting the nose problem early.

Leadership: I set direction quickly, divided the work by stroke, and gave people clear ownership. Once my own stroke was done, I shifted to supporting the open spots, checking joins and freeing up materials. In the final minutes I stayed calm and kept my hands off the area where someone else was finishing, so the last join went in cleanly.", "my_share_percent": 27}
